title: Depression pay and after-hours jam sessions on the road
summary: Speed Webb gigs paid about a dollar and a half or three dollars, but the band jammed in speakeasies until the bus left.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, those days are something, because the Depression was on and we had very little money -- many jobs we would play, in the Speed Webb band -- and I guess Speed was probably robbing us blind, I don't know, but I would hate to accuse him of that, but sometimes we would only get a dollar and a half for playing a dance, if it was a nice piece and the promoter would run away with the money --
Well, if we got $3, that was a good night.
A good night, right. But we sure had a good time, because playing the job wasn't enough for us. That was just the begining, though. After the job,
we would form a jam session, and each time we would find a piano or a little bar, speakeasy bar or someplace, and we could play until daylight if necessary, until the bus leaves for the next town.
